title: ATO releases updated LRBA guidance
full_text:
The ATO has released draft and updated guidance in regards to its handling of limited recourse borrowing arrangements (LRBA), noting their usage may only apply to business real property (BRP) from 10 August.
The regulator released six updated documents, two of which are open for consultation, reflecting the changes made to section 67A of the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) (SIS) Act by the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No 1) Act 2026, which blocked the ability for LRBAs to be used by an SMSF to purchase residential property and redefined property that could be purchased as BRP.
In an update on its website, the ATO stated it had released the amendments it would make to SMSF Ruling (SMSFR) 2009/1 – Self Managed Superannuation Funds: business real property for the purposes of the SIS Act and SMSFR 2012/1 – Self Managed Superannuation Funds: limited recourse borrowing arrangements – application of key concepts.
The changes to SMSFR 2009/1 state it will continue to explain the meaning and application of the term BRP in relation to SMSFs, but noted the changes to the SIS Act dictate whether a fund can acquire real property assets using an LRBA on or after 10 August.
The changes to SMSFR 2012/1 also make note of that shift under law with any references to ‘house’ or ‘houses’ in regards to an LRBA changed to ‘building’ and in examples of where an LRBA can be used changing references to residential house to commercial building or office building.
Consultation on these changes is open until 27 November.
Other guidance updated by the ATO and not subject to consultation includes:
- SMSFR 2009/2, which defines the meaning of ‘borrow money’ under section 67 of the SIS Act, clarifying that where the act allows this for an LRBA, the property must be BRP,
- Practical Compliance Guideline 2016/6 – arm’s-length terms for LRBAs established by SMSFs, which notes residential properties have been excluded since 10 August,
- Taxation Determination 2016/16, which addresses if income of an SMSF will be non-arm’s length if an LRBA was not on arm’s-length terms, and in which references to commercial property have been replaced by BRP, and
- Practice Statement Law Administration 2023/1, which deals with rectification directions for contraventions of the SIS Act, which now refers to commercial property rather than residential property in the context of LRBAs.
ATO SMSF branch director Kellie Grant flagged the release of the updated guidance at the recent SMSF Trustee Empowerment Day 2026 in Sydney last week and added trustees could also access QC107811 on the regulator’s website as another LRBA information resource.
